Neha — drafting list below (will formalize into CSV):

- AWS (EC2, S3, RDS) — cloud compute/storage — processes customer content for hosting; regions: us-west-2, us-east-1
- GCP (BigQuery for analytics job runs) — analytics only; eu-west-1 for EU customers
- Datadog — metrics/tracing/host telemetry — retention per plan; no customer PII in traces
- Sentry — error reporting for service-side crashes — exception traces may include truncated request IDs
- Honeycomb — internal observability for inference pipeline debugging
- Segment (event routing) — only for non-sensitive aggregate telemetry (opt-in in early product tiers)
- Zendesk — support ticketing and attachments (customer-submitted files stored in S3)
- PagerDuty — incident paging (metadata only)
- Intercom — product support chat for trial accounts (includes email addresses, message text)
- Google Analytics / Mixpanel — web analytics; no access to model outputs

Notes:
- We have a number of ephemeral/test integrations in dev that are not used for production customers; those are excluded from the canonical production roster.
- Segment is primarily used in older onboarding flows; we can mark it with limited retention and masking.

I'll populate the CSV columns: vendor, category, data_types, regions, contact, environment (prod/dev), access_controls.

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Quick legal note:
- If any vendor contracts contain narrow NDAs or are resold agreements, call those out in the "notes" column rather than redacting the vendor name entirely. Assessors usually need the vendor name and a short rationale for any missing detail.
- For support ticket attachments: redact any customer-submitted files with PHI before sharing; if redaction isn't feasible, provide meta-data summary instead (filename, type, whether PHI present).

I'll review the final CSV for any contractual sensitivity before it goes to BrightBridge.

-Marissa

Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance

Olivia — attaching our consolidated supplier roster and a short readme that explains scopes and retention. Highlights below and attachments:

Attached: redwood_subprocessors_20260610.csv (canonical roster)
          sig_readme_evidence_20260610.pdf (explanatory notes & retention table)

Summary (selected rows):
- AWS (EC2/S3/RDS) | cloud compute & storage | customer content (model inputs/outputs stored for up to 30 days for debugging) | us-east-1, us-west-2 | infra-ops@redwood.ai
- Datadog | monitoring / traces / metrics | system telemetry, service logs (no raw customer prompts) | global | observability@redwood.ai
- Sentry | error reporting | exception traces; may contain truncated request IDs; customer prompts are masked via sanitizer | global | platform@redwood.ai
- Zendesk | customer support | support tickets, attachments (attachments scanned and redacted when PHI suspected) | us-west-2 | support@redwood.ai
- Intercom | trial-level chat | user messages and email addresses for trial outreach | us-east-1 | product@redwood.ai

Redactions: none for vendor names. Where necessary we redacted specific ticket contents (see readme). If you need a contract or SOC/SIG evidence for a vendor, indicate which vendor and we will surface the supporting docs or a pointer to the vendor's compliance page.

Link to drive folder with raw export and contract pointers: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_supplier_roster

Hi Neha — received, and thank you. The CSV and readme look thorough. Two quick clarifying items for the assessor team:

1) For Datadog and Sentry, can you confirm whether any customer prompt text is ever captured in traces or error payloads (we saw notes about masking/sanitizer). A short sentence per vendor is fine.
2) For Zendesk attachments, do you have a standard workflow for PHI redaction and an owner who can attest to the process?

If you can reply inline to this thread, we'll forward to the assessor and close our intake checklist.

Thanks,
Olivia
